name: Adaptive Mission & Attack-Path Planning Engine
description: Transforms target intelligence, the attack-surface graph, coverage, unknowns, hypotheses, tool capabilities, proof requirements and the mission objective into a dynamic, explainable and continuously re-plannable mission. The mission is a living execution graph of action nodes connected by typed dependencies and conditional branches; replanning emits versioned plan deltas (never full-plan rebuilds) and attack paths are tracked through non-collapsed validation states. It extends Sprint 021/022 proof, Sprint 023/025 tool intelligence & mastery and Sprint 026 adaptive target intelligence without redesigning them.
inputs: MissionObjective (canonical objective; determines coverage priorities, allowed capabilities, validation depth, proof requirements, risk tolerance and completion criteria)
MissionConstraints (scope, authorization context, excluded assets/capabilities, time/execution budgets, rate limits, concurrency, risk threshold, proof/credential/network/retention policies)
Target intelligence state (assets, coverage matrix, unknowns/gaps, hypotheses)
Attack-surface graph (AttackSurfaceGraph assets + typed topology relationships)
Available tool capabilities, tool health and historical effectiveness (Sprint 023/025)
Proof state, evidence refs and candidate findings (Sprint 021/022)
AI proposals (advisory only; converted into structured proposals, never direct execution)
outputs: AdaptiveMission aggregate (state, constraints, execution graph, plan versions, deltas, decisions)

ActionNode execution graph with dynamic dependencies (depends_on, blocks, enables, invalidates, supersedes, alternative_to, requires_evidence/observation/proof) and conditional branches (IF/THEN/ELSE/GOTO/FORK/JOIN/WAIT_FOR_EVIDENCE/REPLAN/STOP)

Ranked, explainable ActionProposal list with decision factors (information gain, hypothesis relevance, coverage improvement, evidence value, proof value, asset criticality, mission priority, tool effectiveness, cost, risk, redundancy, dependency readiness)
PlanVersion history (parent_version, reason, trigger, changed nodes/dependencies, provenance) — fully replayable

AttackPath list scored across explainable dimensions (reachability, evidence strength, criticality, assumptions, validation state, proof availability, risk, objective) with non-collapsed states HYPOTHETICAL/SUPPORTED/VALIDATED/PROVED
EvidenceGap / ProofGap list (minimum action to close each gap)
ToolSelection and ToolFallbackRecord (capability-equivalent substitution, never blind)
PlanCheckpoint for checkpoint/resume without losing intelligence
DecisionRecord answering WHY THIS ACTION / WHY NOW / WHY THIS TOOL / WHAT INFORMATION / WHAT HYPOTHESIS / WHAT EVIDENCE / WHAT PROOF / ALTERNATIVES
engines: DeterministicMissionPlanner (initial explainable plan; deterministic fallback without AI)
PolicyEngine (scope -> authorization -> safety -> risk -> rate-limit gates; immutable scope/authorization)

safe_validation.principle: The planner distinguishes DISCOVERY / VALIDATION / PROOF / IMPACT DEMONSTRATION and never automatically escalates from discovery to destructive exploitation.

persistence.model: normalized entities; no unbounded JSON blobs as the primary persistence model

separation_of_graphs.AttackSurfaceGraph: what exists / what relationships are observed
separation_of_graphs.ExecutionGraph: what HunterX is actually authorized and instructed to execute
separation_of_graphs.rule: the attack graph never directly triggers execution; the planner translates intelligence into authorized actions
